items.title: Foreign Minister Khanal begins bilateral meetings in New York
items.desc: Foreign leaders and senior officials voice solidarity over Nepal’s climate justice position and flood recovery on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly.

items.title: Balendra Shah’s UN appearance draws diplomatic interest in New York
items.desc: Nepal’s prime minister is set to address the General Assembly on climate justice, the Bhotekoshi floods and the concerns of mountain countries.

items.title: Mental wellbeing: What happens when a label becomes your identity?
items.desc: Calling someone ‘weak’, ‘shy’ or ‘smart’ may seem like a simple description. But repeated labels can shape how people understand themselves.

items.title: Rain is coming again. This time, Nepal must be prepared
items.desc: Sound preparation and competent governance can reduce the damage of forecasted heavy rain.

items.title: Gandhi in Babita’s home
items.desc: At Babita’s home, a question once posed by Gandhi looms large: How is the state present in the life of the weakest citizen?

items.title: What the Bhotekoshi flood revealed about Nepal’s health system
items.desc: The emergency phase of the flood has largely been contained, but the most demanding work still lies ahead.

items.title: New hybrid maize variety ‘Saugat’ promises relief for farmers facing extreme weather
items.desc: The variety is on the verge of official certification and release after nearly 11 years of rigorous multi-stage field trials and continuous testing.

items.title: The nurse who wanted to heal Rasuwa
items.desc: Pratima Tamang Lama was a nurse, community worker, and ambitious local leader who dreamed of becoming Nepal’s health minister. The Bhotekoshi flood cut those dreams short.

items.title: Recurring tech failures rattle Nepal’s stock market
items.desc: Repeated breakdowns at Nepse, broker firms, data centres and trading systems are eroding investor confidence and raising concerns over the security of more than Rs4.5 trillion in assets.

items.title: Nepal’s 74-year-old Law Commission remains sidelined in lawmaking
items.desc: The body was created to research, draft and review laws, but most of its bills never reach Parliament, while ministries continue to make legislation that often becomes contentious.

items.title: Nepal unlikely to hold donor conference for reconstruction
items.desc: The government plans to seek funds through bilateral negotiations with major donors.

items.title: Bhat-Bhateni rebuilds 10 stores damaged during Gen Z uprising
items.desc: Despite the destruction and damage to its stores on September 9, 2025, the supermarket chain continued paying over 10,000 employees and began clearing debris within a week.

items.title: Supreme Court orders police not to routinely handcuff people arrested for investigation
items.desc: Handcuffs may be used only after an objective assessment finds a risk of escape, resistance or harm to the detainee or others, the court says.

items.title: Government weighs scrapping VAT on electricity
items.desc: The tax was introduced in the current budget, with a five percent rate for household users and 13 percent for others, but the government is now considering reversing the move.

items.title: Supreme Court dismisses Idemia’s petitions over passport contract
items.desc: The French company had challenged the government’s decision to award the passport-printing contract to German firm Veridos.

items.title: Married at 14, a young mother in Nepal now has nowhere to go
items.desc: Naina left school and eloped at 14. Now a mother of two daughters, she faces pressure to divorce, abuse at home and a family that has stopped speaking to her.

items.title: Textile factory fire in southern Chinese city of Foshan kills eight
items.desc: A ​social media video verified by Reuters showed thick plumes of ​smoke rising from the ​building; a slightly taller building nearby seemed unaffected.

items.title: Government says ending mandatory tender notices in private media does not curb press freedom
items.desc: It tells the Supreme Court that publishing bids through government media avoids duplication, while petitioners argue the change infringes constitutional rights.

items.title: Bus driver set vehicle on fire after passengers got off, police say
items.desc: Police say the 23-year-old driver did not flee after the fire started and suffered burns to more than 90 percent of his body. His motive remains unclear.

items.title: Nepali documentary wins award at film festival in Italy
items.desc: Avash Rijal’s ‘The Witness of Yara’ explores the environmental, cultural and social effects of climate change in Nepal’s Himalayas.

items.title: Why was Nepal’s stock market shut on Monday
items.desc: A ransomware attack at a data centre serving 72 brokers has disrupted trading, leaving investors concerned about the market’s resilience and the security of their data.

items.title: Bus driver sets fire to vehicle in Kathmandu, police say
items.desc: The driver suffered burns to more than 90 percent of his body and is in critical condition, doctors said.

items.title: Xi rolls into Trump summit with China’s trade engine roaring
items.desc: Xi heads into his September 24 meeting with Trump from a position of economic strength, as China’s exports surge and Washington faces pressure to secure an extension of their fragile trade truce.

items.title: Nepse closed after data centre outage disrupts trading
items.desc: A technical failure at the data centre hosting servers used by 72 stockbrokers has forced the Nepal Stock Exchange to suspend Monday’s trading session.

items.title: CIB probes ANFA over alleged financial, match-related irregularities
items.desc: Two ANFA officials arrested as investigators examine Bahrain match arrangements, kit purchases and World Cup ticket sales amid a wider crisis at the football governing body.

items.title: What you should know about the article – and the platform – arguing Washington “groomed” Nepal’s new rulers
items.desc: A US-based website says Prime Minister Balendra Shah and RSP chair Rabi Lamichhane were “cultivated” by an American program. But the document it cites was published in India in March and names leaders from across political parties.

items.title: Swarnim Wagle calls for a reset in Nepal-India ties, says era of anti-India nationalism is over
items.desc: In an interview with The Hindu, the finance minister says Kathmandu wants to focus on trade, connectivity, energy, and reconstruction while constructively addressing contentious issues such as the boundary dispute.

items.title: Money is cheap in Nepal. Businesses still aren’t investing
items.desc: Banks are flush with lendable funds and interest rates are low, yet businesses remain reluctant to borrow and invest, reflecting weak confidence in the economy.
